new_opportunities.title: Director of Pricing and Packaging
new_opportunities.salary_advertised: US Zone 1: $253,300 to $342,700 USD; US Zone 2: $228,000 to $308,400 USD; US Zone 3: $202,600 to $274,200 USD (base pay)
new_opportunities.summary: Define company-wide pricing and packaging across PLG and sales-led motions, design the packaging and monetization architecture for AI-powered products, set pricing governance and experimentation, and lead a small team.
new_opportunities.pricing_focus: SaaS packaging; AI monetization; PLG + SLG
new_opportunities.scope_note: Tagged IC6 internally, but the posting says the role leads and develops a small team. Reports to the Head of Product Marketing.

strategy_updates.pricing_theme: Rebuilding packaging and monetization for AI features (Dash) across self-serve and a growing sales-led business
strategy_updates.current_model: Per-user subscription tiers on dropbox.com/plans (viewed from Canada, so prices shown in CAD): Basic free (2 GB); Plus CA$12.99/month for 1 person (2 TB); Standard at CA$21 or CA$39.50 per user/month depending on billing cycle (team storage from 3 TB); Advanced at CA$33 or CA$39.50 per user/month, 3+ users (team storage from 15 TB); Enterprise by quote. The plans page lists no Dash or AI add-on price.
posting_evidence: Director of Pricing and Packaging, Remote US, first published 2026-11-03 (req R11730); base pay $202,600 to $342,700 by US zone
Reports to the Head of Product Marketing; recruited by the executive recruiting team; internal level IC6 but leads a small team of pricing and packaging staff

Mandate: company-wide pricing and packaging across PLG and SLG, segments, portfolios and geographies, plus 'the next generation of packaging and monetization architecture' for AI-powered products, weighing value, adoption, cost to serve and margin
Set up pricing governance, operating rhythms, KPIs and experimentation; build WTP, usage and unit-economics models; advise senior executives on monetization decisions

Preferred: led a major pricing transformation at a multi-product SaaS company, AI monetization (inference costs, value metrics), conjoint/WTP/elasticity research; mentions 'expanding our sales-led business'

news.summary: The Dash pricing page, which on 2026-10-15 showed Dash for Teams at $15 per user/month (billed yearly) and Dash for Business at $35 per user/month, now redirects to the core plans page, and no Dash price is published.

strategy_updates.interpretation: Dropbox appears to be rethinking how it charges for AI: it took Dash's standalone per-seat prices off its site in late October and posted this director role days later, asking for a new packaging architecture for AI-powered products. Inference: a standalone Dash SKU may be giving way to bundling Dash into the core tiers, or to a usage or credit model, because the posting stresses cost to serve, inference costs and margin. The role also reflects a push to grow the sales-led business alongside self-serve, so the job covers governance and enterprise packaging as well as self-serve price points. Expect a high-visibility mandate with heavy executive and cross-team alignment, and a small team to start.
open_questions: Will Dash be bundled into Standard and Advanced, sold as an add-on, or metered by usage or credits, and who makes that decision?
Pricing sits under Product Marketing rather than Finance or Product: how much decision authority does the role have over list price and discounting for sales-led deals?
How big is the current team, and what experimentation and billing tooling already exists for PLG price tests?
strategy_updates.caveat: The only news item comes from a third-party pricing tracker, not Dropbox. I could not read any earnings commentary today. The plans page was viewed from Canada, so it shows CAD prices and does not say which price goes with which billing cycle.
